stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रातः सन्त्रस्तभोजक्षितिपतिवचसा प्रस्तुते मल्लतूर्ये
सङ्घे राज्ञां च मञ्चानभिययुषि गते नन्दगोपेऽपि हर्म्यम् ।
कंसे सौधाधिरूढे त्वमपि सहबलः सानुगश्चारुवेषो
रङ्गद्वारं गतोऽभूः कुपितकुवलयापीडनागावलीढम् ॥ ७५-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Next morning, the frightened Kamsa ordered the commencement of the wrestling match. The kings took their seats, Nandagopa had also gone to the palace, and Kamsa climbed to the balcony of his palace to watch the happening. Krishna and Balarama, dressed attractively approached the entrance of the arena but were obstructed by the angered great elephant Kuvalayaapeeda.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
prātaḥ santrastabhojakṣitipativacasā prastute mallatūrye
saṅghe rājñāṃ ca mañcānabhiyayuṣi gate nandagope’pi harmyam |
kaṃse saudhādhirūḍhe tvamapi sahabalaḥ sānugaścāruveṣo
raṅgadvāraṃ gato’bhūḥ kupitakuvalayāpīḍanāgāvalīḍham || 75-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पापिष्ठापेहि मार्गाद्द्रुतमिति वचसा निष्ठुरक्रुद्धबुद्धे-
-रम्बष्ठस्य प्रणोदादधिकजवजुषा हस्तिना गृह्यमाणः ।
केलीमुक्तोऽथ गोपीकुचकलशचिरस्पर्धिनं कुम्भमस्य
व्याहत्यालीयथास्त्वं चरणभुवि पुनर्निर्गतो वल्गुहासी ॥ ७५-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna shooed away the elephant by calling it a sinner. The cruel minded and angry mahout prompted the elephant to attack Krishna. The elephant came with great speed and caught Krishna by its tusks. Krishna gave a hard blow to its forehead and Krishna hid between the elephant’s legs and later came out smilingly.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pāpiṣṭhāpehi mārgāddrutamiti vacasā niṣṭhurakruddhabuddhe-
-rambaṣṭhasya praṇodādadhikajavajuṣā hastinā gṛhyamāṇaḥ |
kelīmukto’tha gopīkucakalaśaciraspardhinaṃ kumbhamasya
vyāhatyālīyathāstvaṃ caraṇabhuvi punarnirgato valguhāsī || 75-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
हस्तप्राप्योऽप्यगम्यो झटिति मुनिजनस्येव धावन् गजेन्द्रं
क्रीडन्नापत्य भूमौ पुनरभिपततस्तस्य दन्तं सजीवम् ।
मूलादुन्मूल्य तन्मूलगमहितमहामौक्तिकान्यात्ममित्रे
प्रादास्त्वं हारमेभिर्ललितविरचितं राधिकायै दिशेति ॥ ७५-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna as HE always used to play the sport of disappearing, HE did the same with the elephant also. HE would allow it to catch HIM and suddenly disappeared. The elephant rushed towards Krishna and immediately HE pulled out its life along with its tusks. Below the tusks were some beautiful pearls which Krishna collected and asked HIS friends to make it in to a beautiful necklace and gift it to Radha.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hastaprāpyo’pyagamyo jhaṭiti munijanasyeva dhāvan gajendraṃ
krīḍannāpatya bhūmau punarabhipatatastasya dantaṃ sajīvam |
mūlādunmūlya tanmūlagamahitamahāmauktikānyātmamitre
prādāstvaṃ hāramebhirlalitaviracitaṃ rādhikāyai diśeti || 75-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
गृह्णानं दन्तमंसे युतमथ हलिना रङ्गमङ्गाविशन्तं
त्वां मङ्गल्याङ्गभङ्गीरभसहृतमनोलोचना वीक्ष्य लोकाः ।
हंहो धन्यो नु नन्दो न हि न हि पशुपालाङ्गना नो यशोदा
नो नो धन्येक्षणाः स्मस्त्रिजगति वयमेवेति सर्वे शशंसुः ॥ ७५-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna carried the tusks on the shoulder and walked into the arena with Balarama. Everyone were attracted to the radiance form of Krishna. The people exclaimed that Nandan was highly fortunate, some said it is Yashoda who was fortunate and some declared it is them, who were fortunate in all the three worlds to have the eyes to see Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gṛhṇānaṃ dantamaṃse yutamatha halinā raṅgamaṅgāviśantaṃ
tvāṃ maṅgalyāṅgabhaṅgīrabhasahṛtamanolocanā vīkṣya lokāḥ |
haṃho dhanyo nu nando na hi na hi paśupālāṅganā no yaśodā
no no dhanyekṣaṇāḥ smastrijagati vayameveti sarve śaśaṃsuḥ || 75-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
पूर्णं ब्रह्मैव साक्षान्निरवधिपरमानन्दसान्द्रप्रकाशं
गोपेषु त्वं व्यलासीर्न खलु बहुजनैस्तावदावेदितोऽभूः ।
दृष्ट्वाऽथ त्वां तदेदम्प्रथममुपगते पुण्यकाले जनौघाः
पूर्णानन्दा विपापाः सरसमभिजगुस्त्वत्कृतानि स्मृतानि ॥ ७५-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Not many people had the knowledge that Krishna who lived among the Gopas were the Supreme Bliss and Pure consciousness. At the auspicious time many realised Krishna as Brahman and got their sins relieved instantly. They joyfully narrated all HIS deeds and actions which they remembered.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pūrṇaṃ brahmaiva sākṣānniravadhiparamānandasāndraprakāśaṃ
gopeṣu tvaṃ vyalāsīrna khalu bahujanaistāvadāvedito’bhūḥ |
dṛṣṭvā’tha tvāṃ tadedamprathamamupagate puṇyakāle janaughāḥ
pūrṇānandā vipāpāḥ sarasamabhijagustvatkṛtāni smṛtāni || 75-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
चाणूरो मल्लवीरस्तदनु नृपगिरा मुष्टिको मुष्टिशाली
त्वां रामं चाभिपेदे झटझटिति मिथो मुष्टिपातातिरूक्षम् ।
उत्पातापातनाकर्षणविविधरणान्यासतां तत्र चित्रं
मृत्योः प्रागेव मल्लप्रभुरगमदयं भूरिशो बन्धमोक्षान् ॥ ७५-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: As per Kamsa's order, the boxer Mushtika and the champion wrestler Chanooran started attacking Krishna and Balarama. They created loud noise blowing their fists fiercely, threw up, pushed down, dragged each other many times. Even before death, Chanooran attained bondage and release many times in Krishna's hands.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
cāṇūro mallavīrastadanu nṛpagirā muṣṭiko muṣṭiśālī
tvāṃ rāmaṃ cābhipede jhaṭajhaṭiti mitho muṣṭipātātirūkṣam |
utpātāpātanākarṣaṇavividharaṇānyāsatāṃ tatra citraṃ
mṛtyoḥ prāgeva mallaprabhuragamadayaṃ bhūriśo bandhamokṣān || 75-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
हा धिक् कष्टं कुमारौ सुललितवपुषौ मल्लवीरौ कठोरौ
न द्रक्ष्यामो व्रजामस्त्वरितमिति जने भाषमाणे तदानीम् ।
चाणूरं तं करोद्भ्रामणविगलदसुं पोथयामासिथोर्व्यां
पिष्टोऽभून्मुष्टिकोऽपि द्रुतमथ हलिना नष्टशिष्टैर्दधावे ॥ ७५-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The people exclaimed that Balarama and Krishna are tender bodied and the two wrestlers are tough. They wanted to leave the arena as they did not want to witness that unequal contest. Just then, Krishna caught Chanooran by his arm, whirled him around and threw him dead on the ground. At the same time, Mushtika was crushed to death by Balarama. The remaining wrestlers ran away out of fear.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
hā dhik kaṣṭaṃ kumārau sulalitavapuṣau mallavīrau kaṭhorau
na drakṣyāmo vrajāmastvaritamiti jane bhāṣamāṇe tadānīm |
cāṇūraṃ taṃ karodbhrāmaṇavigaladasuṃ pothayāmāsithorvyāṃ
piṣṭo’bhūnmuṣṭiko’pi drutamatha halinā naṣṭaśiṣṭairdadhāve || 75-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कंसः संवार्य तूर्यं खलमतिरविदन् कार्यमार्यान् पितृंस्ता-
-नाहन्तुं व्याप्तमूर्तेस्तव च समशिषद्दूरमुत्सारणाय ।
रुष्टो दुष्टोक्तिभिस्त्वं गरुड इव गिरिं मञ्चमञ्चन्नुदञ्चत्
खड्गव्यावल्गदुस्सङ्ग्रहमपि च हठात् प्राग्रहीरौग्रसेनिम् ॥ ७५-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Kamsa stopped the drums and not knowing what to do next, ordered to kill Nandagopa, Vasudeva and Ugrasena. He also ordered to also chase away Krishna to a far off place. On hearing the evil minded Kamsa, Krishna leaped like the Garuda from the mountain and reached to Kamsa seated on the throne in the balcony. Kamsa came near Krishna whirling his sword and though he resisted, Krishna caught him forcibly.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kaṃsaḥ saṃvārya tūryaṃ khalamatiravidan kāryamāryān pitṛṃstā-
-nāhantuṃ vyāptamūrtestava ca samaśiṣaddūramutsāraṇāya |
ruṣṭo duṣṭoktibhistvaṃ garuḍa iva giriṃ mañcamañcannudañcat
khaḍgavyāvalgadussaṅgrahamapi ca haṭhāt prāgrahīraugrasenim || 75-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
सद्यो निष्पिष्टसन्धिं भुवि नरपतिमापात्य तस्योपरिष्टात्
त्वय्यापात्ये तदैव त्वदुपरि पतिता नाकिनां पुष्पवृष्टिः ।
किं किं ब्रूमस्तदानीं सततमपि भिया त्वद्गतात्मा स भेजे
सायुज्यं त्वद्वधोत्था परम परमियं वासना कालनेमेः ॥ ७५-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Krishna crushed the joints of Kamsa, pushed him down and jumped on top of him. Immediately Devas, Gods and angels showered flowers on Krishna.
Bhattathiri mentioned here that Kamsa was constantly thinking of Krishna due to fear and because of having focused his mind on Krishna always, he attained Moksha. In the previous birth also, when Kamsa was Kaalanemi, he was killed by Krishna and the remembrance of that paved way for moksha in this birth.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sadyo niṣpiṣṭasandhiṃ bhuvi narapatimāpātya tasyopariṣṭāt
tvayyāpātye tadaiva tvadupari patitā nākināṃ puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ |
kiṃ kiṃ brūmastadānīṃ satatamapi bhiyā tvadgatātmā sa bheje
sāyujyaṃ tvadvadhotthā parama paramiyaṃ vāsanā kālanemeḥ || 75-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तद्भ्रातॄनष्ट पिष्ट्वा द्रुतमथ पितरौ सन्नमन्नुग्रसेनं
कृत्वा राजानमुच्चैर्यदुकुलमखिलं मोदयन् कामदानैः ।
भक्तानामुत्तमं चोद्धवममरगुरोराप्तनीतिं सखायं
लब्ध्वा तुष्टो नगर्यां पवनपुरपते रुन्धि मे सर्वरोगान् ॥ ७५-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Krishna killed eight brothers of Kamsa immediately and offered saluatations to HIS parents. HE made Kamsa's father Ugrasena as king and gave the Yadavas whatever they desired and made them happy. Krishna made friends with Uddhava, the greatest of devotees who received his education from Guru Brihaspati.
Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan who happily stayed in Mathura to protect him from his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadbhrātṝnaṣṭa piṣṭvā drutamatha pitarau sannamannugrasenaṃ
kṛtvā rājānamuccairyadukulamakhilaṃ modayan kāmadānaiḥ |
bhaktānāmuttamaṃ coddhavamamaragurorāptanītiṃ sakhāyaṃ
labdhvā tuṣṭo nagaryāṃ pavanapurapate rundhi me sarvarogān || 75-10 ||
